A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECVC and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reformatting and changes to some comparison anchors.

before.justification: v1 reports original ECVC compression results, computational measurements, component ablations, and finetuning-length experiments in Tables 1–7 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original ECVC experiments in the main text and appendices and adds a feature-perturbation experiment in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The two-reference MNLC/MHLCA architecture and grouped PCFS procedure are retained. The corrected query expression matches the mid-feature input already shown in v1 Figure 3; the explicit PCFS update documents the existing procedure. The shifted-window alternative is discussed without being adopted.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Vimeo-90K and BVI-DVC and evaluate HEVC B–E, UVG, and MCL-JCV under the same compression tasks. The new diagnostic perturbs an internal feature on an existing HEVC sequence without expanding the represented data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes MLVC, RLVC, DHVC, B-CANF, and original DCVC from the IP 32 comparisons. It adds DCVC-TCM to the IP −1/96-frame comparison, DCVC-TCM and DCVC-HEM to all-frame comparisons, and VTM to the MS-SSIM and all-frame comparisons. Reproduced DCVC-DC is retained in appendix Tables 8–11; DCVC-HEM already appeared in v1's 96-frame appendix curves.

E3.justification: The MS-SSIM BD-rate anchor changes from DCVC-TCM to VTM-13.2 LDB, and the all-frame PSNR anchor changes from DCVC-DC to VTM. The new diagnostic adds Gaussian noise to propagated feature F3 and tracks subsequent PSNR and bitrate. Existing training budgets, crops, sequence lengths, and distortion metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds a controlled feature-noise experiment examining how corruption propagates across subsequent frames. Section 3.3 also reports that a shifted-window extension provided no improvement, without quantitative supporting results. The component and finetuning-length ablations in Tables 6–7 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The Gaussian noise distribution specifies an experimental perturbation, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The reported result set changes substantially through comparator additions/removals and replacement of two major comparisons with VTM-relative results. ECVC's MS-SSIM average changes from −36.3% against DCVC-TCM to −56.6% against VTM; these are not same-anchor gains. Under the retained IP −1/96-frame VTM setting, Table 3 changes ECVC's HEVC C/E values from −18.8/−24.9 to −18.9/−26.4 and its average from −29.4 to −29.7. Tables 5–7 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the query definition from FQ(xt) to FQ(yi_t) and refines attention complexity to include channel dimension d, deriving the d/(HW) cost ratio. The normalization theorem and its proof remain mathematically equivalent despite compressed notation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary revise the headline IP −1 advantage over DCVC-FM from 11.1 to 11.5 percentage points, associated in v2 Section 4.2 with all-frame evaluation against VTM. The MNLC and PCFS contributions, novelty claim, and overall state-of-the-art claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that nearby frames exert greater influence than distant frames, using Figure 5 to motivate grouped finetuning. It explicitly discusses interrupted gradients across group boundaries and suggests potential gains from access to official training strategies. The natural-video versus anime limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly names DCVC-DC as the intra-frame codec, although its citation [29] identifies DCVC-FM. It removes DCVC-FM's explicit quality indices 36, 45, 54, and 63, retaining only the bitrate-matching instruction. Hardware, training hyperparameters, appendix architecture details, VTM commands, and promised code availability are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited literature broadens substantially through additions including VCT, MaskCRT, DMVC, ELF-VC, further B-frame and generative-compression work, and attention, optical-flow, BD-rate, and test-condition sources. M-LVC, RLVC, and LLIC citations disappear. The central positioning around limitations of DCVC's temporal context remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 expands and renames Section 3.3, clarifies non-local correlations, makes local wording corrections, subdivides Appendix A, and expands Appendix C from curve references into an explanation of reproduced-baseline comparisons.

P2.justification: v2 converts the document to two columns and extensively rearranges figures, equations, and tables. Main RD plots change from 2×2 grids to horizontal panels; reproduced-baseline tables move into expanded appendix Tables 8–11. Figure 5 is added, Figure 1 is relabeled, and selected RD plots gain comparator curves.

improvement.justification: The new feature-perturbation evidence, clearer complexity analysis, and common VTM anchoring modestly strengthen explanation and comparability while retaining the strongest DCVC comparisons and reproduced baseline. These gains are limited by removed quality-index details and a new reporting inconsistency: Section 4.2 retains the 11.1-point advantage for 96 frames, whereas revised Table 3 implies 11.4 points.
